title: Eclipse season with a weak battery
summary: The Sun is in the orbit plane: the longest eclipses of the year, and the battery has lost capacity.
goals: Understand eclipse seasons (beta angle near zero)
Do an energy budget for one eclipse
Shed non-essential load to keep the main service
situation: 60% of the battery capacity has been lost to failed cells. The satellite enters Earth's shadow in about 5 minutes and stays there almost an hour. If the battery falls to 35% the onboard rule switches the amplifier off and navigation users lose the signal. Do the energy budget and act before the shadow.

steps.text: Switch off the non-essential search-and-rescue payload: pl.sar OFF.
steps.hint: Energy needed = load (W) x eclipse time (h). Compare with the battery's usable capacity.

steps.text: Wait for the eclipse to start.

steps.hint: Use time warp, watch the battery.

failText: The battery fell to the shedding limit: the amplifier would be switched off and users lose the signal.
successText: You kept the service through the eclipse by shedding a secondary payload.
